newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR FALLS UNDER IMPORT PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR FALLS UNDER IMPORT PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar opened Friday weaker against the key U.S. currency, clobbered by rising importer demand and lack of export inflows, foreign exchange dealers said.
"There is more pressure today than we have seen in the past few days and there is no money coming in, or any indication that the central bank will come in to sooth the hot market," one dealer said.
"If they (Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe) don't come in, the pressure will certainly remain high on the Zimbabwe dollar, certainly through the day," he added.
The Zimbabwe dollar opened trade at 11.3500/3600 against the U.S. dollar, before falling 30 minutes later to 11.3800/3900, from its Thursday closing position of 11.3550/3650.

It was being quoted at 18.9500/1900 to pound sterling from its overnight rating of 18.8900/9200. Against the South African rand, the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted at 2.5200/5300 versus 2.5250/5190 and to the German mark at 6.5900/6100 from 6.5650/5730.
